can you delete .desloppify and then run it using the below instructosn - except use it fresh from documents/desloppify locally instead of installing: I want you to improve the quality of this codebase. To do this, install and run desloppify.
Run ALL of the following (requires Python 3.11+):

pip install --upgrade "desloppify[full]"
desloppify update-skill claude    # installs the full workflow guide — pick yours: claude, cursor, codex, copilot, windsurf, gemini

Before scanning, check for directories that should be excluded (vendor, build output,
generated code, worktrees, etc.) and exclude obvious ones with `desloppify exclude <path>`.
Share any questionable candidates with me before excluding.

desloppify scan --path .
desloppify next

--path is the directory to scan (use "." for the whole project, or "src/" etc).

Your goal is to get the strict score as high as possible. The scoring resists gaming — the
only way to improve it is to actually make the code better.

THE LOOP: run `next`. It is the execution queue from the living plan, not the whole backlog.
It tells you what to fix now, which file, and the resolve command to run when done.
Fix it, resolve it, run `next` again. Over and over. This is your main job.

Use `desloppify backlog` only when you need to inspect broader open work that is not currently
driving execution.

Don't be lazy. Large refactors and small detailed fixes — do both with equal energy. No task
is too big or too small. Fix things properly, not minimally.

Use `plan` / `plan queue` to reorder priorities or cluster related issues. Rescan periodically.
The scan output includes agent instructions — follow them, don't substitute your own analysis.

- The raw plan still carries workflow and triage scaffolding as queue items instead of looking like a clean organized execution list. That does not look like a finalized, human-shaped queue.
- The review import clearly injected strong new work, but the live queue is not really prioritizing it. The execution log shows `sync_communicate_score`, `sync_create_plan`, and `review_import_sync` after review import in [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json#L6670), [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json#L6682), and [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json#L6694), yet the live queue still leads with the giant detector bucket `auto/test_coverage` instead of the newly imported architectural and security review findings.
- The top priority cluster is mechanically broad, not strategically decomposed. `auto/test_coverage` is just one 159-issue bucket in [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json#L3334). It mixes very different problems, including plain untested modules and over-mocked tests like `GenerationsPane.test.tsx` in [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json#L287) and [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json#L2939). That is actionable, but not especially thoughtful.
- The security queue also looks mechanically grouped rather than curated. It includes an auth finding against a test mock file, `supabase/functions/_tests/mocks/denoHttpServer.ts`, in [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json#L2615). That suggests the cluster is sweeping in items that likely need human filtering before they deserve top priority.
- There is a mismatch between the strongest subjective findings and the live execution order. The subjective scores say the weakest area is cross-module architecture at `68.0`, and the merged review issues there are concrete and high-confidence, like `shared_neutrality_eroded_into_codebase_hub` and `legacy_supabase_boundary_gate_drift` in [holistic_issues_merged.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/subagents/runs/20260312_195802/holistic_issues_merged.json#L401) and [holistic_issues_merged.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/subagents/runs/20260312_195802/holistic_issues_merged.json#L425). > AGENT

What seems to have gone wrong is that triage was injected, not actually executed.

- The plan shows triage placeholders, not a completed triage product. In [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json#L84) through [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json#L89), the queue still literally contains `triage::observe`, `triage::reflect`, `triage::organize`, `triage::enrich`, `triage::sense-check`, and `triage::commit`.
- The execution log confirms those were auto-injected during review import, not produced by a real organize run. In [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json#L6694), `review_import_sync` says `triage_injected: true` and lists the injected triage IDs at [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json#L6821). That is the clearest signal that the workflow advanced state, but did not actually perform a thoughtful triage pass.
- Because organize did not really happen, the old detector buckets kept control of the live queue. The biggest example is `auto/test_coverage` in [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json#L3334), which is just a 159-issue detector cluster with `user_modified: false` and a generic action line. That is not a curated execution plan.
- The imported review issues themselves are stronger than the queue. For example, the cross-module architecture issues in [holistic_issues_merged.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/subagents/runs/20260312_195802/holistic_issues_merged.json#L401) and [holistic_issues_merged.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/subagents/runs/20260312_195802/holistic_issues_merged.json#L425) are high-confidence, codebase-level, and well evidenced. A real organize pass should have considered moving some of that work ahead of “add tests in 158 files.”
- The auto-clusters also were not cleaned up enough before being prioritized. The security cluster includes `_tests/mocks/denoHttpServer.ts` in [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json#L3509), which suggests the cluster is still detector-shaped rather than human-filtered.
- The queue still contains raw workflow scaffolding at the top, like `workflow::communicate-score` and `workflow::create-plan` in [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json#L6) and [plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json#L7). That is another sign the plan never got normalized into a real execution order after review import.

My inference from this is:

The system imported good review findings, then performed a sync step that injected triage placeholders and preserved preexisting auto-clusters, but it never actually ran the observe/reflect/organize process that should have converted those 56 review issues into a thoughtful, leverage-based queue.

So the failure mode is not “bad review.” The failure mode is “review succeeded, organize never truly materialized.”

Yes. The specific bug is a shell-quoting bug in the `organize` stage’s generated skip-recording command, not a problem with your repo.

Evidence is in [organize.log](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/triage_runs/20260312_214829/logs/organize.log#L1118):
- It generates a nested command like:

  - `done <<'"'\"'\"'EOF'\"'\"'`

That leaves the shell in an unbalanced quote state, and zsh fails immediately with:
- `zsh:28: unmatched '` at [organize.log](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/triage_runs/20260312_214829/logs/organize.log#L1146)

- `organize` is generating invalid zsh/bash wrapper commands for bulk `plan skip --permanent` calls

> AGENT

Yes. I looked in the local tool source, and the answer is:

- `organize` and `sense-check` are absolutely supposed to use the CLI tools directly.
- The `Documents/desloppify` subdirectory is not the reason this happened.
- What went wrong is later in the queue/lifecycle logic, not in whether the subagents could call the tool.

Evidence:

- The triage runner explicitly creates a helper script so subagents use the exact local checkout and interpreter. See [`orchestrator_codex_pipeline.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/orchestrator_codex_pipeline.py#L94).
- The prompts explicitly tell sense-check/organize subagents to run commands like `plan cluster update` and `plan cluster show` via that helper. See [`stage_prompts_sense.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/stage_prompts_sense.py#L63).
- Your own run logs prove it actually did that. `organize.log` shows real `run_desloppify.sh plan skip ...` and `plan cluster update ...` commands being executed successfully.

So the “tools didn’t work because they’re in a subdirectory” theory does not fit the source or the logs. The helper is specifically there to make the subdirectory setup work.

What I think actually happened:

- Triage did use the tools.
- Triage did create and enrich the manual clusters.
- But after triage completed, `next` switched back to objective execution because of the work-queue phase selector.

The key source is [`snapshot.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/snapshot.py#L164):
- if there are any `objective_items`, `_phase_for_snapshot(...)` returns `PHASE_EXECUTE` immediately
- only if there are no objective items does it surface postflight review/workflow/triage items

And in the same file, execute phase returns only `objective_items`, not the review/triage items. See [`snapshot.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/snapshot.py#L189).

That matches what we saw:
- triage completed
- manual clusters existed in the plan
- but `desloppify next` still surfaced `auto/test_coverage`

So the likely failure mode is:
- triage writes the plan correctly
- but the active work queue prefers planned objective backlog over the triaged review-driven plan

There is also a second hint in your current state:
- `queue_order` in [`plan.json`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json#L5) contains the raw review IDs
- but the live queue is showing objective auto-clusters instead

That suggests the triage data exists, but the work-queue projection is not honoring it the way you expected.

Can this be replicated?
Yes.

A clean reproduction is:
1. Run subjective review import.
2. Run `desloppify plan triage --run-stages --runner codex`.
3. Confirm triage and complete it.
4. Run `desloppify next`.

If objective backlog exists, the current queue code appears to prefer objective items and can jump straight to something like `auto/test_coverage`, even though the triage just produced a much better manual plan.

So my conclusion is:
- tool usage during organize: yes, working as designed
- broken because tool is in subdirectory: no
- likely bug: work-queue phase/order logic after triage completion, not the triage subagents themselves

If you want, I can trace the exact queue code path further and point to the specific function that should probably be changed so triaged manual clusters actually drive `next`.

- And in the same file, execute phase returns only objective items, not review/triage items. See [`snapshot.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/snapshot.py#L189).
- Planned objective IDs come from tracked plan IDs intersected with live objective IDs. See [`schema/__init__.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/schema/__init__.py#L302).

So the practical effect is:

- the moment the plan still tracks live objective backlog like `auto/test_coverage`
- `next` enters execute phase
- and the triaged review-driven work stops driving the queue, even though the triage clusters exist

So no, this is not “just switch back to triage mode.”
There does not appear to be a hidden persistent mode flag to flip.

It is a queue-selection rule:
- objective backlog present => execute phase wins

That’s why I wasn’t fully definite earlier: there were three plausible failure points:
1. subagents not using tools
2. triage not writing plan state
3. work queue ignoring the written triage plan

After tracing the source, it looks like `3` is the real one.

So if you want the behavior you expected, the likely fix is in the queue logic, not in changing a mode:
- either change `_phase_for_snapshot(...)`
- or change what counts as planned objective work after triage
- or promote the triaged clusters into the execution-visible set in a different way

No. `next` is not showing backlog item `#1`.

`next` only shows `execution_items`, while backlog is a separate surface. That is explicit in [`selection.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/selection.py#L49):
- `visibility == BACKLOG` returns `snapshot.backlog_items`
- otherwise it returns `snapshot.execution_items`

So if something is appearing as `#1` in `desloppify next`, the tool considers it part of the execution queue, not the backlog.

What’s happening here is subtler:
- the triage data is definitely still present in [`plan.json`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json#L4001)
- but the queue engine is deciding that objective work is the active execution phase
- and once that phase is selected, `next` shows objective execution items like `auto/test_coverage`

That phase switch is in [`snapshot.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/snapshot.py#L164):
- if `objective_items` exist, it returns `PHASE_EXECUTE`
- and execute phase returns only `objective_items` at [`snapshot.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/snapshot.py#L189)

So the problem is not “backlog items are mislabeled as #1.”
The problem is:
- the execute-phase selector is choosing the objective queue
- which effectively sidelines the triaged review plan, even though that plan data still exists

So yes, we should respect the triage order in spirit.
But in the current code, `next` is not using that triage order as the active execution surface once objective backlog is present.

what is the pahse selector? what dos that even mean?

> AGENT

The phase selector is the bit of code that decides what kind of work `desloppify next` should show right now.

In this codebase, that function is [`_phase_for_snapshot`](#/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/snapshot.py:164). On every `next` run, it recomputes the current queue “phase” from the live plan/state. It is not a manual mode toggle.

Its rule order is:

1. initial subjective review
2. execute objective work
3. scan
4. postflight review
5. postflight workflow
6. postflight triage

The important line is here:
[`snapshot.py`](#/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/snapshot.py:176)

If there are any planned objective items, it returns `PHASE_EXECUTE`. Then `next` shows only those execute items:
[`snapshot.py`](#/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/snapshot.py:201)

So “phase selector” just means:
- “which bucket wins when there are multiple kinds of work available?”

In your run, objective backlog existed, so the selector chose `execute`, and `next` surfaced `auto/test_coverage` instead of the triaged review plan.

Why objective backlog still counted as planned is the second half of the problem. That comes from [`planned_objective_ids`](#/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/schema/__init__.py:302), which treats any objective IDs tracked anywhere in the plan as active planned work. “Tracked” includes:
- `queue_order`
- `skipped`
- `overrides`
- cluster `issue_ids`
- cluster step `issue_refs`

See [`tracked_plan_ids`](#/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/schema/__init__.py:286).

So the plain-English root cause is:

- triage wrote good cluster data into the plan
- but `next` does not say “show the triage plan now”
- it says “if any planned objective backlog exists, show execute items”
- and your auto clusters still made that condition true

That is why I keep saying this is not a simple switch-back-to-triage-mode problem. The selector recomputes from rules every time.

[`review_coverage.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/review_coverage.py)
and in triage sync:
[`triage.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/sync/triage.py)

`triaged_ids` is only a set of review-style IDs. It does not include mechanical detector issues like coverage, unused, exports, security, etc.

So the honest answer is:

- Were these `auto/*` items triaged? No, not formally.
- Were they just “not inserted into the queue”? Also no.
- They are a separate queue population: objective backlog.

What triage did:
- analyze the imported review findings
- create manual clusters for those review findings
- record those review IDs in `epic_triage_meta.triaged_ids`

What triage did not do:
- absorb the objective backlog into that same plan
- replace `auto/test_coverage` with a triaged version of those mechanical issues

Why `next` shows them:
- the phase selector sees planned objective backlog and chooses execute phase first in [`snapshot.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/snapshot.py:164)
- execute phase returns only objective items in [`snapshot.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/snapshot.py:189)
- triage even has a banner path that says objective work can keep triage pending in [`plan_triage.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/plan_triage.py:82)

So the root distinction is not “triaged but hidden.”
It is “never in the triage scope to begin with.”

They are the same broad data shape, but not the same workflow class.

In state, both are just open issues. But the code splits them into two categories:

- review issues: `detector` is `review`, `concerns`, or `subjective_review`
- objective issues: everything else, like `test_coverage`, `unused`, `exports`, `security`

That split happens in the queue code in [snapshot.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/snapshot.py:97) and [snapshot.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/snapshot.py:89).

Your expectation would make sense if triage were a general “plan all open work” step. But in this code, triage is narrower:
- it only tracks open review issues
- it records only review IDs in `triaged_ids`

You can see that in [review_coverage.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/review_coverage.py:16) and [apply.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/apply.py:149).

So the current behavior is:

- triage decides which review findings become active manual clusters
- objective issues are handled separately by the execute queue
- `next` does not wait for triage to bless objective issues one by one

That is why `auto/test_coverage` can become the live `#1` item even after triage completed.

So the answer to your direct question is:
- different kind of workflow thing: yes
- same raw issue object underneath: mostly yes
- does triage currently decide whether objective issues become active queue items: no, not in this implementation

> AGENT

Yes. I can answer this more precisely now.

Short version:

- `triage`: these objective items are partially collected, but not actually shown to the triage model/subagent
- `subjective review`: they are considered only indirectly, as score/context, not as explicit queue candidates to accept/reject

The clearest root cause is in triage input vs prompt construction.

What the code does:
- `collect_triage_input(...)` explicitly splits open issues into:
  - `open_issues` = `review` + `concerns`
  - `mechanical_issues` = everything else
- That is in [`prompt.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/prompt.py:88) and [`prompt.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/prompt.py:113)

So your understanding was reasonable: the system does gather the mechanical/objective issues.

But then the bug/omission is here:
- `build_triage_prompt(si)` only renders:
  - existing clusters
  - new/resolved review issues
  - recurring dimensions
  - all open review issues
  - dimension scores
  - previously dismissed review IDs
- It never renders `si.mechanical_issues`

That is in [`prompt.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/prompt.py:366)

So for triage, the answer is:

- Are `auto/test_coverage`-style items collected? Yes
- Are they actually presented to the triage agent to decide “make active queue item vs not”? No

That is the strongest root cause I’ve found so far.

On the subjective side:

- objective backlog is definitely considered as a gating signal
- but not as explicit per-item triage material

Evidence:
- subjective visibility computes `has_objective_backlog` from planned open non-subjective issues in [`subjective.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/policy/subjective.py:80)
- if objective backlog exists, stale/under-target subjective items are suppressed/evicted from plan in [`subjective.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/policy/subjective.py:35)
- synthetic subjective queue items are built from `dimension_scores` and open review counts, not from the explicit mechanical issue list, in [`synthetic.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/synthetic.py:160)

So subjective review “sees” them only in aggregate:
- they affect scores
- they affect whether subjective reruns are deferred
- they are not individually surfaced for “should we tackle this now?”

So the most accurate answer is:

- Your expectation is valid.
- The current implementation does not fully do that.
- The mechanical/objective items are collected for triage, but then dropped before prompt generation.
- After that, the queue phase selector prefers execute-mode objective backlog anyway.

If you want the exact one-line diagnosis:

`TriageInput` has `mechanical_issues`, but `build_triage_prompt()` ignores it, so the triage agent never actually sees the objective backlog it was presumably meant to reason about.

> DEVELOPER

and is the distinction between them and the stuff we triage clean? are they they same type of thing?  Where would it make sense for us to present them to the user? I think they should probably be backlogged items that the triage step must consider

> AGENT

No, the distinction is not especially clean.

At the data level, they are basically the same kind of thing: open issues in state with an `id`, `detector`, `status`, `summary`, `detail`, and so on. The split is workflow-level, not schema-level.

The current split is:
- review-side triage input: `review` + `concerns`
- objective backlog: everything else like `test_coverage`, `unused`, `exports`, `security`

You can see that in [`prompt.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/prompt.py:14) and [`prompt.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/prompt.py:88). That boundary is leaky, because `concerns` is already a synthesized judgment layer over lower-level detector output, so semantically these are not two completely different species of work.

The strongest sign the design wanted this to be unified is that `TriageInput` already has a `mechanical_issues` field in [`prompt.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/prompt.py:22), but `build_triage_prompt()` never renders it in [`prompt.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/prompt.py:366). So the code already gathers the objective backlog for triage, then drops it before the agent ever sees it.

Where it makes sense to present them:
- During `reflect`, as a `Mechanical Backlog Context` section. That is the stage where prioritization decisions belong.
- In `organize`, only if reflect decided a mechanical cluster should be promoted into active execution.
- In `next`, as backlog, not as immediate execution, until triage has explicitly considered them.

So your proposed model is the one that fits the current architecture best:
- objective/mechanical items should remain backlog items by default
- triage should be required to consider them
- triage should decide whether to promote, defer, merge into a manual cluster, or leave backlogged

That would be much cleaner than the current behavior, where:
- triage only really acts on review findings
- objective items are still allowed to seize `next` afterward via the phase selector in [`snapshot.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/snapshot.py:164)

So my view is:
- same underlying type of thing: mostly yes
- clean separation today: no
- best UX/design: yes, treat objective clusters as backlog candidates that triage must explicitly consider before they become top execution items

If you want, I can sketch the exact code change path to make that happen with minimal disruption.

Overall Assessment

  The design is sound and well-motivated. The main things I'd tighten:

  1. Name the function that changes: planned_objective_ids() → either modify it or introduce
  executable_objective_ids() alongside it.
  2. State the pre-triage behavior explicitly: Empty queue_order = nothing in next unless
  autofix-eligible.
  3. Clarify promoted_ids reuse vs new metadata fields.
  4. Resolve the "visible in both next and backlog" contradiction for autofix items.
  5. Default for un-mentioned backlog items in triage: state that silence = "leave in backlog."

> AGENT

I’m folding those constraints in directly. Concrete choices: introduce `executable_objective_ids()` rather than overloading `planned_objective_ids()`, make empty `queue_order` mean no detector work in `next` except eligible autofix items, reuse `promoted_ids`, treat unmentioned backlog items as “leave in backlog”, and keep auto-promoted autofix items out of backlog while they are active.

> AGENT

Overall, that list is good. The main sense-checks I’d make are:

1. `executable_objective_ids()` was the right choice.
It keeps `planned_objective_ids()` available for broader “plan-tracked” semantics and avoids overloading one function with two meanings.

2. Point 2 needs one wording tweak.
“Empty `queue_order` = nothing in `next` unless autofix-eligible” is too broad.
What’s true now is:
- no detector-created objective work appears in `next`
- but workflow/review/subjective items can still appear if their phase is active

So I’d phrase it as:
- “Empty `queue_order` means no detector-created objective work in `next`, unless autofix-eligible.”

3. `promoted_ids` is the shakiest part.
Right now the implementation reuses `promoted_ids` only indirectly through `move_items()`, and that helper only records IDs when moved to `top`.
So:
- `plan promote foo top` is recorded in `promoted_ids`
- `plan promote foo bottom|before|after ...` is not

That means the current code does not fully satisfy “reuse promoted_ids as promotion metadata” unless we define `promoted_ids` very narrowly. If you want all explicit promotions audited consistently, this should be tightened.

4. The autofix contradiction is resolved correctly.
Active autofix-eligible items show in `next` and are not duplicated in backlog. That part is coherent.

5. “Silence = leave in backlog” is implemented and should stay explicit.
That’s now in the triage prompt text, and it’s important. Without it, the agent will infer too much.

The one extra thing I’d sense-check beyond your list:

- `backlog` currently still includes workflow items like `workflow::run-scan` in some states, because backlog is “everything not in execution,” not “detector backlog only.”
If you want backlog to mean only deferred detector-created work, that still needs tightening. Right now it’s semantically broader than the name suggests.

So my short verdict:
- 1, 4, 5: solid
- 2: good, but wording should be narrower
- 3: not fully clean yet in the implementation
- extra risk: backlog still mixes in workflow/postflight items, which may or may not be what you want

so will the traige staage have the tools/data to know what it needs to do?

> AGENT

Mostly yes, for the behavior we just implemented.

What it has now:

- It sees the review issues as before.
- It also now sees a `Mechanical backlog context` section built from `mechanical_issues` in [prompt.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/prompt.py).
- The prompt explicitly says:
  - backlog items are backlog by default
  - promote only the ones that should become active now
  - silence means “leave in backlog”
- The runner instructions now expose the relevant commands:
  - `desloppify backlog`
  - `desloppify plan promote ...`
  - cluster/show commands
  Those are in [stage_prompts_instruction_shared.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/stage_prompts_instruction_shared.py) and [stage_prompts_instruction_blocks.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/stage_prompts_instruction_blocks.py).

So at a workflow level, yes: triage now has both the data and the tool needed to decide what to pull into the active queue.

The main limitation is this:

- the mechanical backlog context is still a summarized prompt section, not a fully structured backlog planning model
- so the agent can consider backlog and promote items, but it is not yet forced through a strict “review every backlog cluster and mark keep/promote/defer” schema

So my honest read is:

- enough to work correctly: yes
- fully robust / impossible to misunderstand: not yet

If you want the next hardening step, it would be to make `reflect` or `organize` emit an explicit `backlog promotion decisions` section that validation checks, instead of relying only on prompt wording.

> DEVELOPER

and are the review issue and mecahnical backlog differnet versions of the same thing?

> AGENT

Yes, basically.

They are the same underlying kind of object in state: open issues with the same general shape like `id`, `detector`, `status`, `summary`, `detail`, `file`, `confidence`.

The distinction is workflow classification, not schema.

Right now the split is:
- review issues: detectors like `review` and `concerns`
- mechanical backlog: everything else like `test_coverage`, `unused`, `exports`, `security`, `smells`

That split is made in [prompt.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/prompt.py), where `collect_triage_input()` separates:
- `open_issues`
- `mechanical_issues`

So they are not two different data models. They are two categories of issue that the system treats differently.

That’s also why this bug existed in the first place:
- the system was already collecting both
- but only the review side was truly driving triage and queueing

So the clean mental model is:

- same base issue type
- different queue/triage policy layers on top

If you want, the next cleanup would be to rename the triage fields so this is more obvious, something like:
- `review_issues`
- `objective_backlog_issues`
instead of the more ambiguous `open_issues` and `mechanical_issues`

type.\n+- Feature-owned entrypoints such as `features/resources/*` or `features/shots/*` should host the real implementation. If a component depends on app contexts, feature hooks, or workflow-specific behavior, move it out of the UI primitive root.\n - `shared` can host neutral contracts and infrastructure, but feature orchestration, repository logic, and Supabase-backed workflows should live in the owning `domains`, `features`, or `tools` module.\n - When two areas need the same type, extract that type into a neutral shared contract file instead of importing from one concrete widget package into another.\n - Prefer folder entrypoints (`index.ts`) for reusable shared component packages so callers import the package boundary instead of deep implementation files.\n+- When a feature or domain owns a surface, keep the implementation in that owner and leave any legacy `shared/*` path as a documented compatibility shim only. > DEVELOPER

I have a concern about the direction.                                                              
                                               
  Looking at the consumers being updated — character-animate, join-clips, travel-between-images,     
  image-generation — MediaGallery is genuinely shared across 4+ tools. Moving it from shared/ to     
  features/gallery/ doesn't clarify ownership, it just makes other tools depend on a sibling feature 
  instead of on shared/. That's arguably worse — it creates a cross-feature dependency where there
  was a clean shared import.

  The decomposition into smaller hooks/components is fine in principle (if the original was a bloated
   monolith), but it could be done in place under shared/components/MediaGallery/ without relocating.
   That would give you the smaller-file benefits without the ownership confusion.                    
                                                                  
  So the concern is:
  - Decomposing a monolith into focused modules — good
  - Relocating genuinely shared code into one feature's directory — creates misleading ownership and 
  cross-feature imports                                                                             
  - Net +5000 lines before the shared/ originals are fully gutted — risky mid-flight state to comm

> AGENT

Your concern is valid. I think the current direction is wrong on the ownership question.

- `MediaGallery` is used as a cross-tool primitive, not a gallery-feature-private surface. The current consumers include [ResultsGallery.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/tools/character-animate/pages/components/ResultsGallery.tsx), [JoinClipsResults.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/tools/join-clips/pages/components/JoinClipsResults.tsx), [VideoTravelVideosGallery.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/tools/travel-between-images/components/VideoGallery/VideoTravelVideosGallery.tsx), and shared callers like [MediaGalleryItem.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/components/MediaGalleryItem.tsx). That does not support `features/gallery` as the true owner.
- Moving the canonical implementation under [MediaGallery.tsx](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/features/gallery/components/MediaGallery/MediaGallery.tsx) while other tools import it creates cross-feature dependencies and weakens the architectural signal.
- The decomposition work is still useful. Splitting hooks/components and adding behavior coverage was good. The ownership relocation is the questionable part.
- The current “feature owner + shared compat shims” state is a risky midpoint. It is workable short-term, but I would not want to keep it as the final shape.

My recommendation:
- Stop following the queue literally on this specific ownership claim.
- Keep the decomposition and tests.
- Move the canonical `MediaGallery` implementation back to `shared/components/MediaGallery`.
- Keep `features/gallery` limited to gallery-feature compositions like `GenerationsPane` and feature-specific wrappers, not as the owner of shared gallery infrastructure.
- Treat this review item as partially mis-triaged: the real fix is “decompose shared gallery surface,” not “make gallery feature own shared gallery.”

So I would not continue deeper down the current ownership direction without correcting course first. If you want, I’ll undo the canonical move to `features/gallery`, preserve the smaller-module refactor and tests, and then continue the rest of the queue from that corrected baseline.

No. The current live state is not honoring the intended `scan -> subjective review -> score -> triage` handoff.

Current state:
- `desloppify next` shows `subjective::abstraction_fitness`
- `desloppify plan queue` shows only the 20 subjective items
- but the plan itself already has `triage::observe`, `triage::reflect`, `triage::organize`, `triage::enrich`, `triage::sense-check`, `triage::commit` at the very front of [`plan.json`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json)
- and the CLI simultaneously says `46 new review work item(s) not yet triaged`

So the queue state is contradictory: triage is pending and first in `queue_order`, but `next` is still surfacing subjective items.

The updated score did land:
- strict score is `84.4/100`
- I found `sync_communicate_score` in the execution log and `workflow::communicate-score` in [`plan.json`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json)
- so the score checkpoint/communication machinery did appear in state, but it is not what the live queue is surfacing now

Why this is happening in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify`:
- The real problem is in [`snapshot.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/snapshot.py).
- `_phase_for_snapshot(...)` does not follow `queue_order` directly. It picks a phase from synthesized partitions.
- Its postflight priority is:
  1. `scan`
  2. `postflight_assessment_items`
  3. `postflight_workflow_items`
  4. `triage_items` when review backlog is present
- So if subjective items still exist, they win before workflow and triage.
- And [`synthetic.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/synthetic.py) keeps generating subjective items whenever dimensions are below target.
- Result: after subjective review import creates new review findings and injects triage stages, the queue can still stay stuck in subjective mode, because `postflight_assessment_items` never goes empty.

So the root cause is:
- triage stages are present in plan state
- score communication is present in plan state
- but the phase selector in `snapshot.py` gives subjective postflight higher priority than workflow/triage
- therefore `next` does not advance to the triage recovery step even though it should

One more detail:
- I did start the triage recovery with override, but your interruption aborted that run before it completed
- so there is no completed new triage pass yet

My read is that the intended order is correct, but the implementation is wrong at the phase-selection layer. The fix is likely:
- when new review items are imported and `triage::*` is present, triage should preempt subjective items
- or subjective items should be suppressed once untriaged review backlog exists after a review import

If you want, I can patch `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify` so `next` actually follows that order.

> AGENT

Yes, that’s close, but I’d separate “pregenerated” from “wrongly visible.”

- Pregeneration itself is intentional here. `sync_subjective_dimensions()` injects later `subjective::*` IDs into `queue_order` early, and `triage::*` is also pre-injected. The phase system is supposed to hide later stages until their turn.
- The actual leak is visibility: `build_subjective_items()` currently turns every below-target dimension into a live postflight review item, not just placeholder or stale ones.
- That means once postflight starts, `postflight_assessment_items` can stay non-empty forever, so `_phase_for_snapshot()` never advances to score or triage.

So the root cause is not just “they were pregenerated.” It is:
1. under-target dimensions are being treated like active review work
2. the phase selector always gives subjective postflight priority over workflow and triage

The cleaner model is exactly what you’re suggesting:
- generate or surface postflight subjective work only when we actually enter postflight
- and only for dimensions that truly need review now: unassessed or stale
- not for fresh under-target dimensions

In code terms, the immediate fix is:
- keep `queue_order` as the long-lived plan
- make `build_subjective_items()` stale-only for postflight visibility
- optionally stop injecting under-target `subjective::*` IDs into `queue_order` as live work and keep them as optional backlog/cluster data instead

That matches `centralize-postflight-pipeline.md` much better, because that task says postflight injects `stale dimension reruns`, not generic below-target reminders.

what's the best and most robust strategy? Why not do that? Even that may be a patch though :)

> AGENT

The most robust strategy is:

1. Make postflight injection boundary-owned.
   Only create live postflight subjective work when the explicit execution queue actually drains.

2. Limit live subjective postflight work to:
   - unassessed dimensions
   - stale dimensions with `needs_review_refresh`
   Not fresh under-target dimensions.

3. Keep fresh under-target dimensions as score/backlog data, not active queue items.
   They can live in an optional backlog cluster like `auto/under-target-review`, but they should not block `score -> triage`.

4. Treat `queue_order` as the live queue, and never let later-phase items become visible just because they were pre-seeded.

Why I did the smaller patch first:
- it fixes the concrete bug with minimal blast radius
- it matches the lifecycle docs immediately
- it avoids ripping through `sync_subjective_dimensions`, subjective auto-clusters, and migration behavior in one shot

So yes, your suggested direction is better than the local guard I just added. The guard is a safe stopgap. The cleaner fix is to move stale-rerun generation to the postflight boundary and stop treating fresh under-target dimensions as live review work at all.

If you want, I’ll do the full version in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify` next:
- change `sync_subjective_dimensions()` so under-target IDs are not injected into the live queue
- keep them as optional backlog/cluster data
- add lifecycle tests proving `scan -> subjective review -> score -> triage`
- then rerun the queue in this repo to confirm it advances correctly

> AGENT

Yes. Root cause is clear now.

It failed because `sense-check` content subagents rewrote several steps to include speculative future paths, and the final validator rejected those paths because they do not exist on disk.

The 4 unique bad paths introduced in the latest run were:
- `src/shared/settings/runtime/`
- `src/tools/image-generation/pages/ImageGenerationToolForm.tsx`
- `src/tools/image-generation/pages/useImageGenerationToolForm.ts`
- `src/shared/lib/shots/shotAssociationChecks.ts`

Where they came from:
- `settings-runtime-hardening` content batch invented `src/shared/settings/runtime/` as a concrete destination in [sense_check_content_12.log](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/triage_runs/20260313_114620/logs/sense_check_content_12.log)
- `image-generation-ownership-and-coverage` content batch explicitly says it “replaced vague wording with executable targets” and injected `ImageGenerationToolForm.tsx` plus `useImageGenerationToolForm.ts` in [sense_check_content_16.log](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/triage_runs/20260313_114620/logs/sense_check_content_16.log)
- `media-gallery-association-logic` content batch injected `src/shared/lib/shots/shotAssociationChecks.ts` in [sense_check_content_17.log](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/triage_runs/20260313_114620/logs/sense_check_content_17.log)

Why this keeps happening:
- The content stage is trying to make steps “executable without guesswork”.
- In doing that, it sometimes turns a valid architectural intent into a specific not-yet-existing file path.
- The validator only checks paths after all edits are applied, so the bad mutations land in the plan and then the run fails at the end.

So the actual bug is not in your repo and not “missing script”.
The bug is in the `sense-check` content workflow design:
- it allows invented future file paths in step text
- but its validation model requires referenced paths to already exist

That is a contract mismatch.

The evidence is strongest in [sense_check_content_16.log](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/triage_runs/20260313_114620/logs/sense_check_content_16.log), where it explicitly celebrates adding a “concrete wrapper file” that does not exist.

If you want, I can patch `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify` so content/sense-check stops introducing speculative paths and only references:
- existing files
- existing directories
- or generic package surfaces without fake filenames

> AGENT

Yes. The root issue is in the `sense-check` content prompt contract in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify`, not in `reigh`.

What was happening:
- The content prompt explicitly tells the subagent to make vague steps “executor-ready” and replace vague extraction language with more specific targets in [stage_prompts_sense.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/stage_prompts_sense.py).
- But it did not forbid naming not-yet-existing files.
- The validator then rejects any nonexistent path via the enrich/sense-check path checks in [enrich_checks.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/validation/enrich_checks.py) and [enrich_quality.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/validation/enrich_quality.py).

So the subagent was doing exactly what the prompt encouraged:
- turning “add a tool-owned wrapper” into fake concrete files like `ImageGenerationToolForm.tsx`
- turning “move under shared settings” into `src/shared/settings/runtime/...`
- turning “extract helper in shared shots” into `shotAssociationChecks.ts`

Those are good implementation ideas, but they are invalid as step text because the validator requires referenced paths to already exist. That’s the contract mismatch.

I patched that directly:
- Added explicit prompt rules: only reference paths that already exist on disk; if a new file is warranted, reference the existing parent package/directory instead of inventing a filename in [stage_prompts_sense.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/stage_prompts_sense.py)
- Added the same prohibition for structure/cascade mutations there too
- Tightened the bad-path failure message so future failures point at speculative paths immediately in [enrich_quality.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/validation/enrich_quality.py)
- Added regression coverage in [test_triage_runner.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/plan/test_triage_runner.py)

Verification passed:
- `pytest -q /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/plan/test_triage_runner.py -q`
- `pytest -q /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/test_lifecycle_transitions.py /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/review/test_work_queue_plan_order_and_triage.py -q`

So the root cause is: prompt encourages speculative concretization, validator forbids speculative paths. I fixed the prompt to match the validator. If you want, I can now rerun `sense-check` in `reigh` against the patched local checkout.

Let's get to the bottom of what went wrong/was confusing here

> AGENT

I’m tracing the remaining confusion points end-to-end: why the run looked stuck, why `sense-check` kept failing, and why `next` now crashes even though triage is effectively ready to commit.

> AGENT

What went wrong was three separate problems layered together.

First, the main triage failure:
- `sense-check` content subagents were encouraged to make steps “executor-ready” by naming concrete targets.
- But the validator requires every referenced path to already exist on disk.
- So the subagent kept inventing future files like `ImageGenerationToolForm.tsx`, `useImageGenerationToolForm.ts`, and `src/shared/settings/runtime/...`, and validation failed at the end.
- That was a tool bug in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify`, not a repo problem.

I traced that to:
- prompt side: [stage_prompts_sense.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/stage_prompts_sense.py)
- validation side: [enrich_checks.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/validation/enrich_checks.py) and [enrich_quality.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/validation/enrich_quality.py)

I patched the prompt contract so sense-check now:
- only references paths that already exist
- describes new modules via an existing parent package/directory instead of inventing filenames

That fix held in practice:
- the latest run [20260313_122154](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/triage_runs/20260313_122154/run_summary.json) confirmed `sense-check`

Second, the thing that is confusing right now:
- `desloppify next` and `desloppify plan queue` are crashing
- this is a different bug, also in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify`

Root cause:
- [playbook.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/playbook.py) still includes `value-check` in `TRIAGE_STAGE_LABELS`
- but `TRIAGE_STAGE_PREREQUISITES` no longer has a `value-check` entry
- `sense-check` already absorbed value-check as a subagent, and [constants.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/constants.py) reflects that
- so queue/guardrail code hits `KeyError: 'value-check'`

That is why the tool feels contradictory:
- the actual run succeeded
- the plan state has only `observe`, `reflect`, `organize`, `enrich`, `sense-check`
- but the queue progress renderer still thinks `value-check` is a standalone stage

Third, what’s actually next:
- triage is effectively ready for `commit`
- but the CLI surface is currently broken by the `value-check` playbook bug

So the clean diagnosis is:
1. `sense-check` dead-path failures were caused by a prompt/validator mismatch
2. that is now fixed
3. the remaining confusion is a separate stale-stage bug in `playbook.py`
4. the intended next step is triage commit, but `next` cannot render it until that bug is fixed

If you want, I can patch the `value-check` crash in `Documents/desloppify` now so `desloppify next` works again and shows the real next step instead of crashing.

> AGENT

Fixed in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify`.

Root cause was exactly the stale standalone `value-check` stage in [playbook.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/playbook.py). `value-check` had already been folded into `sense-check` in [constants.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/constants.py), but the playbook still treated it as a separate stage, so `compute_triage_progress()` could hit a missing prerequisite entry and crash `desloppify next` / `desloppify plan queue`.

I removed `value-check` from the canonical stage list and manual stage commands in [playbook.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/triage/playbook.py), updated the stale workflow docstring in [command.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/command.py), and cleaned up the affected tests in [test_triage_jump_back.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/plan/test_triage_jump_back.py), [test_triage_fold_confirm.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/plan/test_triage_fold_confirm.py), and [test_triage_logging.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/plan/test_triage_logging.py).

Verification:
- `pytest ...test_triage_snapshot.py ...test_triage_stage_policy_direct.py ...test_triage_jump_back.py ...test_triage_fold_confirm.py ...test_triage_logging.py`
- Result: `30 passed`
- The active CLI import is still local: [desloppify/__init__.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/__init__.py)

`desloppify next` now works again in `reigh`. Current live queue is:
- `auto/subjective-review`

So the crash is fixed. The tool is now surfacing real queue state again instead of dying on triage progress rendering.

Yes. The root cause is now clear, and it’s two separate mechanisms that looked like one bug.

1. The original post-review handoff bug is in [plan_sync.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/importing/plan_sync.py).
After a review import, it does this in order:
- `_sync_review_delta(...)` appends the new `review::...` findings to `plan["queue_order"]`
- then it checks `if live_planned_queue_empty(plan):`
- only then would it run `reconcile_plan(...)`

That means the boundary check happens too late. By the time it asks “is the queue empty?”, it has already made the queue non-empty with the newly imported review items. So the postflight reconcile is skipped.

Why that matters:
- `reconcile_plan(...)` is the thing that runs `sync_subjective_dimensions(...)`, workflow injection, and triage injection
- because it was skipped, the plan kept stale synthetic `subjective::...` queue IDs around and did not cleanly transition into `score -> triage`

This is not accidental. The old behavior is explicitly locked in by tests:
- [test_review_importing_support_direct.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/review/test_review_importing_support_direct.py#L441)
- [test_review_importing_support_direct.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/review/test_review_importing_support_direct.py#L470)

Those tests literally assert that review import should not purge subjective IDs and should skip reconcile when the queue is considered mid-cycle.

2. The current subjective rerun request is partly real.
In [state-typescript.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/state-typescript.json), several dimensions are now marked:
- `needs_review_refresh: true`
- `refresh_reason: review_issue_wontfix`

Examples:
- `abstraction_fitness`
- `api_surface_coherence`
- `convention_outlier`
- `naming_quality`

That comes from [resolution.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_state/resolution.py): when review findings are resolved as `wontfix`, the corresponding dimension is marked stale on purpose.

So the full story is:

- We did complete the subjective review.
- The first confusion happened because review import skipped the postflight reconcile and left stale synthetic subjective queue state behind.
- Then later, triage/skip decisions legitimately marked some dimensions stale again via `review_issue_wontfix`, which created a new subjective rerun request.

So:
- “Did we already do subjective review?” Yes.
- “Why did it still look like we hadn’t?” Because the import-time boundary logic is wrong.
- “Why is there subjective work now?” Because some dimensions were subsequently marked stale by `wontfix` review dispositions.

The main bug to fix upstream is the first one:
- review import should decide whether to run postflight reconcile based on the pre-import boundary state, not after appending new review findings into `queue_order`.

If you want, I can patch that next in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify`.

> DEVELOPER

is there something inelegant or poorly structured or complicated  about the postflight stuff that all these issues keep happening? I think the decision for what's in the queue should happen when we ENTER post/preflight mode?

> AGENT

Yes. The postflight design is more complicated than it should be, and that complexity is exactly why these issues keep surfacing.

The structural problem is that postflight queue state is not boundary-owned. Instead, it is recomputed from several overlapping mechanisms:

- review import mutates `queue_order`
- reconcile may or may not run depending on a late emptiness check
- synthetic queue builders regenerate subjective items from state
- stale markers in state can resurrect review work later
- `next` then chooses a phase from synthesized partitions rather than from a single committed postflight plan

That means the system is trying to answer “what should be in the queue now?” in too many places.

Your instinct is right: the clean design is to decide the postflight queue when you enter the postflight boundary.

The robust model is:

- `scan` finishes
- enter `review`
- subjective review runs
- import scores/findings
- enter `score`
- enter `triage`
- materialize the live postflight queue for that phase transition
- from then on, `next` reads that queue, it does not re-infer it from scattered state

That is much cleaner than the current model, where:
- review import appends findings
- synthetic subjective items are derived separately
- triage stages are injected separately
- phase selection tries to sort it all out afterward

Why the current approach is brittle:
- it mixes source-of-truth and projection
- `queue_order` is partly authoritative and partly ignored
- synthetic items are regenerated continuously instead of being boundary decisions
- “stale” subjective state and “covered by imported review” are allowed to conflict

So yes: the elegant fix is to make entry into preflight/postflight a commit point.

At that boundary, the system should:
- clear obsolete synthetic items from the previous phase
- generate exactly the queue for the new phase
- persist it
- let `next` consume that persisted queue directly

In other words:
- phase transition decides queue contents
- queue rendering should not be doing lifecycle policy inference on every call

That would remove most of the failure modes we just chased:
- stale subjective placeholders surviving import
- triage being injected but not surfaced
- postflight review items reappearing unexpectedly
- queue behavior depending on whether reconcile happened before or after appending findings

So my answer is:
- yes, the current postflight structure is inelegant
- yes, it is over-distributed and too dynamic
- yes, deciding the queue when entering pre/postflight is the better design

The patch we’ve been making improves symptoms. Your proposed boundary-owned queue design is the real fix.

no functonlaity hsims, just data shims if necessary - also:   ---                                                                                                                                  
  Sense-Check: Postflight Pipeline Plan                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                       
  The bug diagnoses are accurate                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                       
  The four concrete bugs are real and correctly identified:                                                                            
  1. Stale subjective::... IDs — reconcile/prune logic doesn't catch them after review import completes their purpose                  
  2. Post-review reconcile skip — sync_plan_after_review_import() appends review::... IDs before checking live_planned_queue_empty(),  
  so the boundary check sees a non-empty queue and skips reconcile_plan()                                                            
  3. Reviewed dimensions re-requested — needs_review_refresh fires immediately after import because open findings mark dims stale      
  4. Queue instability — dynamic re-synthesis on every next invocation means phase can flicker                                       
                                                                                                                                       
  Concern 1: The solution is much larger than the bugs require                                                                         
                                                                                                                                       
  The four bugs could be fixed with targeted changes:                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                       
  - Bug 2 (the most impactful): Move the emptiness check before mutations in sync_plan_after_import(). ~5 lines changed.               
  - Bug 1: Add a prune step in the review-import boundary handler that removes subjective::... IDs for covered dimensions.           
  - Bug 3: Add a cooldown check in build_subjective_items() that skips dimensions covered by the current import cycle (import metadata 
  already tracks which dims were assessed).                                                                                            
  - Bug 4: Make _phase_for_snapshot() respect the persisted lifecycle_phase more strongly when it exists, rather than re-inferring from
   partition contents.                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                     
  The plan proposes rebuilding the entire queue lifecycle model to fix these. That's a valid architectural choice, but the             
  risk-to-reward ratio should be acknowledged.                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                       
  Concern 2: Persisted materialized queue introduces a new divergence failure mode                                                     
  
  Currently, the queue is rebuilt from canonical state on every invocation. This is the cause of the instability bug, but it's also a  
  safety net: the queue always reflects reality. If you persist a materialized queue as the authoritative source, you need invalidation
   logic for when state changes outside boundary transitions:                                                                          
                                                                                                                                     
  - User manually edits .desloppify/plan.json                                                                                          
  - External tool modifies state
  - A scan runs mid-postflight (e.g., --force-rescan)                                                                                  
  - Unexpected crash leaves partial state                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                       
  The plan doesn't address invalidation. You'd need either: (a) a version/hash check that detects stale materialized queues, or (b)    
  acceptance that the materialized queue can be wrong until the next boundary.                                                         
                                                                                                                                       
  Concern 3: "Materialize once" vs. boundary trigger mechanics                                                                         
  
  The plan says "materialize the live queue for that phase once" but doesn't clearly define what triggers boundary transitions in the  
  new model. Currently live_planned_queue_empty() is the trigger, and it requires synthesis to evaluate. If the new model still uses 
  queue-emptiness as the trigger, you still need synthesis to detect boundaries, which partially undermines the "materialize once, stop
   re-synthesizing" premise.                                                                                                         

  Suggestion: Be explicit about the trigger. Something like: "A boundary transition fires when the last non-synthetic item in the      
  materialized queue is completed/skipped. The transition handler then materializes the next phase's queue." This removes the need for
  synthesis at the trigger point.                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                     
  Concern 4: The lifecycle phases lose granularity                                                                                     
  
  The plan proposes: scan → review → score → triage → execute                                                                          
                                                                                                                                     
  The current code has: PHASE_REVIEW_INITIAL, PHASE_ASSESSMENT_POSTFLIGHT, PHASE_WORKFLOW_POSTFLIGHT, PHASE_TRIAGE_POSTFLIGHT,         
  PHASE_REVIEW_POSTFLIGHT, PHASE_EXECUTE, PHASE_SCAN                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                       
  Key distinction being lost: PHASE_REVIEW_INITIAL (first-ever review, no scores exist) vs. PHASE_ASSESSMENT_POSTFLIGHT (re-review of  
  stale/under-target dims after a cycle). These have different rendering, different item selection, and different user expectations.
  The plan folds both into "review." If that's intentional, it needs explicit handling for the initial-review case.                    
                                                                                                                                     
  Also: PHASE_REVIEW_POSTFLIGHT (triage findings surfaced for review) is distinct from assessment and from initial review. The plan    
  doesn't mention this phase at all.
                                                                                                                                       
  Concern 5: Section 6 conflates two things                                                                                            
  
  _phase_for_snapshot() should not be the place where lifecycle decisions are made                                                     
                                                                                                                                     
  Currently _phase_for_snapshot() does two things:                                                                                     
  1. Inference: What phase are we in? (reads state signals)                                                                            
  2. Policy: Given ambiguity, which phase wins? (priority rules)
                                                                                                                                       
  The plan correctly wants to eliminate (2) by making the phase explicit/persisted. But (1) is still needed as a fallback for old data 
  and edge cases. The section should acknowledge that _phase_for_snapshot() becomes a "read persisted phase, with legacy fallback      
  inference" function rather than being eliminated.                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                       
  Concern 6: Section 5 cooldown mechanism may be simpler than proposed                                                                 
  
  The plan proposes a last_postflight_review_cycle or review_refresh_blocked_until_phase_exit marker. But the import already records   
  which dimensions it assessed. A simpler approach:                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                       
  - build_subjective_items() checks if a dimension was covered in the most recent import (already in state as                          
  dimension_scores[dim].last_import_cycle or derivable from import metadata)
  - If the current lifecycle phase is still in the same postflight cycle as the import, skip it                                        
  - No new persistent field needed; just a comparison against existing data                                                            
                                                                                                                                       
  What's solid                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                       
  - Section 3 (fix the review import boundary check ordering) — correct and necessary                                                  
  - Section 4 (separate triage inputs from live queue) — good separation of concerns                                                 
  - Section 7 (normalize stale synthetic cleanup) — the scattered pruning is a real maintenance burden; a shared function is the right 
  call                                                                                                                                 
  - Section 8 (backward compat via lazy migration) — correct approach, aligns with the project's data migration policy                 
  - Test plan — thorough and well-structured; covers the lifecycle contract, boundary transitions, and regression cases

  Phase A (targeted fixes, low risk): Fix bugs 1-4 directly (~100-200 lines changed). This unblocks the reigh issues immediately.      
                                                                                                                                     
  Phase B (architectural, higher risk): Pursue the materialized queue + explicit lifecycle model as a follow-up. This gives you time to

  4. Clarity on whether _phase_for_snapshot() survives as a legacy fallback or is fully replaced

Implemented in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify` with targeted changes, not a queue-architecture rewrite.

What changed:
- [plan_sync.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/importing/plan_sync.py): review import now captures the boundary state before queue mutation, prunes covered `subjective::...` IDs on trusted imports, and runs postflight reconcile from the pre-import boundary instead of the post-mutation queue.
- [review_import.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/sync/review_import.py): extended the import sync result so covered-subjective pruning is tracked cleanly.
- [synthetic.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/synthetic.py): live subjective work is now only unassessed or explicitly stale dimensions; fresh under-target scores no longer become queue items, and same-cycle `review_issue_*` refreshes are suppressed during workflow/triage.
- [snapshot.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/snapshot.py): persisted workflow/triage phase now wins more strongly instead of letting assessment items opportunistically override it.
- [inputs.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/inputs.py): passes plan context into subjective synthesis so the same-cycle suppression can use lifecycle phase.

Verification:
- `pytest -q ...test_review_importing_support_direct.py ...test_sync_split_modules_direct.py ...test_lifecycle_transitions.py ...test_work_queue_plan_order_and_triage.py`
- Result: `77 passed`

Its [.desloppify/plan.json](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/.desloppify/plan.json) still has `refresh_state.lifecycle_phase = "review"`, so `desloppify next` there is still showing subjective items from stale persisted state. The code is fixed; that repo state needs the next real lifecycle boundary to normalize under the new rules.

> AGENT

Findings:

1. The phase resolver in the plan is underspecified for real post-triage states. In [curious-hopping-stallman.md](/Users/user_c042661f/.claude/plans/curious-hopping-stallman.md#L78), `_resolve_reconcile_phase()` only derives `triage_postflight`, `workflow_postflight`, `review_initial`, `assessment_postflight`, or “retain current / scan”. It never explicitly resolves `review_postflight`, even though the plan introduces that phase at [curious-hopping-stallman.md](/Users/user_c042661f/.claude/plans/curious-hopping-stallman.md#L55) and snapshot still uses it today in [`snapshot.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/snapshot.py). That leaves a real gap for the “triage completed, review findings now surface” state.

2. Step 4 is too aggressive about skipping `auto_cluster_issues()`. At [curious-hopping-stallman.md](/Users/user_c042661f/.claude/plans/curious-hopping-stallman.md#L185), the plan says to skip both `sync_subjective_dimensions()` and `auto_cluster_issues()` whenever workflow is predicted. But [`pipeline.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/sync/pipeline.py) uses `auto_cluster_issues()` as broader plan maintenance, not just subjective refresh decoration. Skipping it wholesale risks stale cluster metadata and stale detector cluster state at exactly the boundary where you want cleanup to be most reliable.

3. Step 6 likely over-simplifies the same-cycle suppression rule. At [curious-hopping-stallman.md](/Users/user_c042661f/.claude/plans/curious-hopping-stallman.md#L241), the plan removes the timestamp/import-cycle comparison and relies only on “past review phase” plus `refresh_reason.startswith("review_issue_")`. That will wrongly suppress older legitimate stale review refreshes from prior cycles, because phase alone cannot distinguish “stale from this import cycle” from “stale carried forward from an earlier cycle.” The current timestamp/audit check is ugly, but it is carrying real disambiguation that the proposed version drops.

4. The caller migration around `coarse_phase_name()` needs to be more explicit. At [curious-hopping-stallman.md](/Users/user_c042661f/.claude/plans/curious-hopping-stallman.md#L111), the plan says to remove `coarse_phase_name()` and replace it with `coarse_lifecycle_phase(plan)`. But several current call sites consume `snapshot.phase`, not just `plan`, such as [`queue_progress.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/helpers/queue_progress.py). That is fixable, but the current writeup implies a simpler substitution than the codebase actually supports.

What looks solid:

- Step 1 is good. Centralized synthetic cleanup is a real improvement.
- Step 2’s goal is right. Removing the pipeline dependency on `queue_context()` / snapshot is worth doing.
- Step 3 is directionally right. Snapshot should become a persisted-phase reader with legacy fallback.
- Step 5 is a clean refactor target and low risk.

My recommendation:
- Keep the overall direction.
- Tighten Step 2 so `_resolve_reconcile_phase()` explicitly covers `review_postflight` and execute/scan fallthrough.
- Narrow Step 4 to skip only subjective-specific injection work, not all auto-cluster syncing.
- Keep some notion of import-cycle correlation in Step 6; don’t collapse it to phase-only logic.

So the plan is good, but not decision-complete yet. The main unresolved pieces are `review_postflight` resolution, the scope of the Step 4 skip, and preserving same-cycle vs prior-cycle stale distinction.
